assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells. Rows with no options use a blank cell or [:].
assertions.evidence: Options kept as three separate columns: '| Fragile | Insured Value | Handling |' with mostly blank cells, not collapsed into single map column

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method present. Options are constructed manually in method body: 'if (Boolean.TRUE.equals(fragile)) opts.setFragile(true);'

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Dimensions column uses list format: '| [20, 15, 10] |' and parameter 'List<Integer> dimensions'

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
assertions.evidence: One row uses value set: 'Same rate all carriers | EU | express | 3.0 | [30, 20, 15] |         |               |          | {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} | 12.00'

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: Only one @TableTest method present. Single table mixes base rates (rows 1–8), dimensional weight (row 9), surcharges (rows 10–13), and carrier equivalence (row 14)

assertions.text: Weight and cost parameters use BigDecimal (not double or String). Dimensions use Integer or int.
assertions.evidence: Parameters: 'BigDecimal weight, List<Integer> dimensions, ... BigDecimal expected' and method signature uses these types

assertions.text: Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column is 'Scenario' with values like 'EU standard light', 'EU express medium', etc.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names describe conditions: 'EU standard light', 'Fragile surcharge', 'Dimensional weight override', 'Oversize surcharge'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
assertions.evidence: Column header: '| Cost?' as the rightmost column

assertions.text: Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers ('shippingZone', 'weightKg', 'dims')
assertions.evidence: Column headers use business language: 'Scenario', 'Region', 'Service', 'Weight', 'Dimensions', 'Fragile', 'Insured Value', 'Handling', 'Carrier', 'Cost?'

assertions.text: Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body contains if statements: 'if (Boolean.TRUE.equals(fragile))...', 'if (insuredValue != null)...', 'if (handling != null)...'

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest annotation present on method, no @DisplayName or @Description to order

assertions.text: Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: Method name 'calculateShippingCost' is generic. No @DisplayName annotation present to provide descriptive title

assertions.text: Output contains no TestNG syntax: no @DataProvider, @Test(dataProvider=...), Object[][], or TestNG imports (org.testng.*).
assertions.evidence: Only imports from 'org.junit.jupiter' and 'org.tabletest.junit'; no TestNG imports or @DataProvider present
